MRK.rationale: Merck's fundamental health is deteriorating on multiple fronts. Q1 2026 GAAP EPS collapsed to -$1.72 (vs. +$2.01 in Q1 2025), driven by a ~$9B Cidara charge and ~$5.8B Terns R&D impact, which together represent nearly $15B in one-time costs that will depress near-term earnings. While operating cash flow remained positive ($3.92B, +56.7% YoY), the balance sheet eroded with total equity declining ~$6B in a single quarter. The franchise is dangerously concentrated: Keytruda accounts for over half of sales, and its patent expires in 2028, creating a structural cliff that the company is scrambling to address through expensive M&A. GARDASIL declined 22% in Q1 2026, and a late-stage trial (LITESPARK-012) failed, narrowing pipeline optionality. Valuation is at extreme highs relative to own history: PE diluted at 36.1x (maximum of 365-day range), P/B at 7.0x (maximum), and ROE at 19.5% (below the 20-40% range). The forward P/E of ~48x (Yahoo) embeds aggressive pipeline conversion assumptions that have not been proven. The earnings yield of 2.8% is 191bp below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.71%, meaning the equity does not compensate holders for risk. The stock has rallied 66.5% over one year, and much of the positive pipeline optionality appears priced in. The upcoming August 4 earnings could serve as a near-term catalyst, but given the structural risks and stretched valuation, the risk-reward is unfavorable.
